newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Worried Russia calls for dialogue in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Worried Russia calls for dialogue in Albania.

text.p: Russia said on Monday it was deeply concerned by events in Albania and called on all sides to put aside "narrow political ambitions" in the interests of peace, Interfax news agency said.
Deputy foreign minister Alexander Avdeyev told Interfax that it was vital now to stop weapons proliferating and to try to limit the risk of more bloodshed.

"The foreign ministry...appeals to all political forces in Albania to refrain from narrow political ambitions and to go over to dialogue and search for ways to establish civil peace and agreement in the country," Avdeyev said.
"In Moscow we would like a mechanism to be found as soon as possible to limit the influence of the street on the political situation".
A state of emergency and nationwide curfew went into force in Albania on Monday as parliament elected President Sali Berisha to a second five-year term in office.
At least 12 people were killed at the weekend after crowds in several southern towns raided weapons depots and went on a rampage of burning and looting.
